introduction.name: Introduction
introduction.text:
Start-up sequence initiated...

Greetings, Pioneer. You have been tasked with establishing a new outpost on an uninhabitted planet. The environment isn't ideal for organic life, but it has been identified to be rich in resources. For that reason, you, an artificial sapience (AS) operating a robotic frame, have been deployed to manage the new outpost and development into an industrial base.

I am your assistant AI. I am not as advanced an intelligence as you, but I will help guide you through the process using the data provided in my database. To keep you on track as you get started, most of the recipes and machine schematics have been locked except for the most critical. As you learn the basic tasks and production, more advanced technologies will be opened up.

For the sake of minimizing initial costs, we are practicing In Situ Resource Utilization (ISRU) to establish this outpost. You are provided the most basic machinery in order to process local resources and develop more advanced machinery. To improve chances, we have established our outpost in a region detected to have deposits of iron, copper, and ice.

To get started, go to the nearby deposit of iron ore, mine some samples, and return here. You will then be introduced to your first stage of refining ores and minerals. Before you go out, remember to activate your stirling radioisotope generator (SRG). It will be your source of energy until you are able to create other methods of energy generation.
introduction.hint:
Mine iron ore by selecting it from the Harvest option menu and click the "Harvest" button.

Don't forget to activate the SRG by clicking the "Inactive" button and start generating energy.

basic ore refinement pt1.name: Basic Ore Refinement Part I
basic ore refinement pt1.text:
Scanning mineral... Iron ore confirmed...

Well done, Pioneer. Iron ore is the most critical resource for creating machines and structures. Iron is very durable for its weight, though it's not the best metal. It will be good enough for now until you gain access to more advanced metals and alloys like steel, titanium, or aluminum.

To get started, deposit your iron ore into your smelter-extruder and set it to produce iron wire. Your smelter-extruder is your first critical machine for ISRU and establishing your industrial base. It melts down the ore and outputs it as thin iron wire. It isn't the most efficient process for refining ore and much of it is wasted, but it will work as a start until you construct a more efficient furnace.
basic ore refinement pt1.hint: Make sure that your Smelter-extruder is set to the Iron Wire recipe and activate it. It will continuously consume iron ore and produce wire.

basic ore refinement pt2.name: Basic Ore Refinement Part II
basic ore refinement pt2.text:
Confirmed iron wire produced...

Another machine provided to you for ISRU is the component printer. It accepts wires, filaments, and other thin flexible materials and uses it to craft solid components via additive construction. I have unlocked for you the recipes for iron plates and small iron gears which will be necessary for many machines. I recommend setting it to create metal plates as they will be needed soon. If you start getting low on iron wire, remember to collect more iron ore and insert it into the smelter-extruder.

Another common metal that will be useful is copper. Copper is highly conductive and important for electronics. It isn't as good a conductor as gold, but given it is far more common, it serves the function well enough. A copper ore deposit has also been detected near the landing site. Mine some copper ore and put it in the smelter-extruder to produce copper wire.
basic ore refinement pt2.hint:
Set the Harvest option to copper ore and harvest. Once you have copper ore, set the smelter-extruder to produce copper wire.

You can also set the component printer to produce iron plates while collecting and processing copper.

electromagnetism pt1.name: Electromagnetism Part I
electromagnetism pt1.text:
You have also produced copper wire. Well done, Pioneer.

To begin producing more advanced parts for machines, you will need to create motors that can convert electrical current into rotational mechanical energy. But before we can accomplish that we will need to create permanent magnets.

By winding wire into a coil and passing a current through it, you will create a magnetic field. Then if you expose iron to a powerful magnetic field and heat it, its domains will align and become magnetized.

Make sure you have enough iron plates and copper wire and build a magnetizer. Also make some iron rods so they may be used in the magnetizer to produce magnets.
electromagnetism pt1.hint: Under the build menu, select the magnetizer machine. Make sure you have 10g of iron plates and copper wire, then click the "Build" button. Also set the component printer to produce iron rods.

electromagnetism pt2.name: Electromagnetism Part II
electromagnetism pt2.text:
Iron rods confirmed... Magnetizer confirmed...

Now that you have constructed the new machine, creating permanent magnets is simple. Just provide it with iron rods, and it will magnetize them. Don't worry if the magnets are too large. They can be easily divided into smaller magnets. No matter how small pieces you break a magnet into, they will all have north and south poles. There are no known means of creating magnetic monopoles.
electromagnetism pt2.hint: Set the new magnetizer to produce magnets, and don't forget to activate it. If you are getting low on energy, deactivate some of your other machines.

electromagnetism pt3.name: Electromagnetism Part III
electromagnetism pt3.text:
Magnets produced... Well done, Pioneer.

Magnets will be useful in many industrial and technological functions. By creating a coil of wire and placing a magnet in the middle of it, you can make an electric motor. By either passing a current through the coil, the magnet will then rotate to align with the generated magnetic field. And by rotating the magnet within the coil, it will induce an electric current in the wire. Electric motors are your first major technological advancement towards creating your industrial base.

The fourth and last machine you have been provided with for your ISRU mission is the parts assembler. It can be programmed with schematics and will produce machine parts with fine precision. I have unlocked its electric motor for you. Provide it with iron plates, copper wire, and magnets to begin crafting motors.
electromagnetism pt3.hint: You will need iron plates, copper wire, and the magnets you just produced and make them in the parts assembler.

automated mining.name: Automated Mining
automated mining.text:
Now that you can make motors, it is time to get the machines to do work for you and save yourself from having to harvest the raw resources yourself.

The schematics for an automated miner have been unlocked for you.
automated mining.hint: The miner is an expensive machine but worth it for to work it will save you. It costs 20g iron plates, 10g small iron gears, and 10g electric motors.

power generation.name: Power Generation
power generation.text:
Now that you are constructing and using more machines, the SRG will not be able to support all of them at the same time. So you will need to build more generators.

Motors convert electrical energy to rotational motion, but the reverse is also possible. Moving the magnet within a coil of wire will induce electrical current. A common natural resource to produce renewable energy is wind, and given what parts are able to create right now, this is now possible. Create some iron plates and rods, copper wire, and electric motors then build a wind turbine.
power generation.hint: You will need 5g of iron plates, 10g of iron rods, 5g of copper wire, and 5g of electric motors. You may need to deactivate some of your machines so some of these resources aren't automatically being crafted.

mechanical batteries.name: Mechanical Batteries
mechanical batteries.text: You started with a hich capacity lithium rechargeable to store your generated energy, however if you want to expand your energy storage, you will not be able to construct any more without the ability to extract and process lithium. For now, you will need to find another method to store and release energy. With access to electric motors which can function for both converting to and from electricity and mechanical energy, you can use a heavy weight to store gravitational potential energy by storing energy by raising the weight then releasing it as it drops when it is needed.
mechanical batteries.hint: You will need 5g of iron plates, 10g of iron rods, 5g of copper wire, and 5g of electric motors. You may need to deactivate some of your machines so some of these resources aren't automatically being crafted.

from thin air.name: From Thin Air
from thin air.text:
A critical technology you will need is the ability to create polymers like plastic. Unfortunately, there are no signs of fossile fuels detected on this planet, so you won't be able to synthesize polymers from resources like crude oil.

Fortunately, there is a plentiful source of carbon, a vital element for polymers, in the very atmosphere of the planet. Carbon dioxide (CO2). For the first step of creating polymers, you will need to collect CO2 from the atmosphere using an atmospheric condensor.
from thin air.hint: An atmospheric compressor will cost 10g iron plates, 10g copper wire, 5g small iron gears, and 5g electric motors.

mineral processing.name: Mineral Processing
mineral processing.text:
As introduced earlier, the machines provided to you are relatively inefficient, and you will need more advanced machines that will work more efficiently getting more out of it and producing less waste. Though you also need to keep in mind that you need to "live off the land" and use every resource available. Not only does that mean nothing goes to waste but you also need to find value in resources available to you that you would otherwise consider worthless. Everything is made of basic elements, and with advanced enough technology, you should be able to make something out of anything. And if its advanced enough, not even the elements would be able to restrict you.

Your next step is to find a use for the rock that is in such great abundance around you. To process the stone, one machine you can use is one that can crush stone and other minerals into finer aggregate like gravel and sand. You have the schematics to build a crusher.
mineral processing.hint: Build a crusher using 10g of iron plates, 5g of small iron gears, and 5g of electric motors.

breaking rocks.name: Breaking Rocks
breaking rocks.text:
With the crusher, you can pulverize minerals into aggregate. You will be instructed what to do with ores, but for now you will only use stone which will be crushed into gravel and sand.

Mine some rock from the regalith around you and put it in the crusher.
breaking rocks.hint: Select rock from the harvest menu and collect rock. Then activate the crusher to produce gravel and sand.

obliterating rocks.name: Obliterating Rocks
obliterating rocks.text: Gravel can have some uses later on, but you will need to crush them further into a fine dust to use them for construction.
obliterating rocks.hint: Select the pulverize gravel recipe in the crusher and produce 10g of stone dust.

mixology on the rocks.name: Mixology on the Rocks
mixology on the rocks.text: Now you will need to combine fluids and powders to create mixtures. Build a mixer machine and set it to mix clay combining stone dust and water. The resulting clay slurry could be used for making ceramics later, but for now it will function as a mortar to be used in bonding bricks into walls and other structures.
mixology on the rocks.hint: Build a mixer with 10g iron plates, 5g small iron gears, and 5g electric motors. Then set it to perform the mix clay recipe to combine stone dust with water. You may need to collect ice and melt it in the smelter-extruder.

masonry.name: Masonry
masonry.text:
In order to build proper constructions, especially structures that are durable or heat resistant, you will need to build out of stone. While there is no shortage of rock around you, it isn't convenient to build with especially as you mine it out of the ground. Since stone isn't as malleable as metal, it will need to be carved and sculpted into uniform bricks.

Before you can build your stone carver machine, you will need to make some blades to cut stone with. You can print them in the component printer. Once you have built the carver, set it to carve stone bricks. It will also produce stone dust as waste.
masonry.hint: Iron blades can be made in the component printer. A stone carver will require 10g iron plates, 5g iron blades, and 5g electric motors.

induction pt1.name: Induction Part I
induction pt1.text:
By passing alternating currents through coils of wire, you can generate fluctuating magnetic fields that induce eddy currents, and when ferromagnetic metals such as iron are exposed to them, they will generate heat. Because of this property, induction heating is both safe as it only heats specific materials and is also efficient compared to other methods such as resistive heating.

The recipe for crafting induction coils has been unlocked for the parts assembler. Craft some of them before building the next critical industrial machine.
induction pt1.hint: Induction coils require copper coils and iron plates and are made in the parts assembler. Make 20g of them.

induction pt2.name: Induction Part II
induction pt2.text: The induction smelter is the first industrial smelter you will construct and also your first step to moving from relying on your starting machine setup. It uses heat generated by induction but needs walls of stone bricks to resist and hold in the intense heat.
induction pt2.hint: The induction smelter requires 10g iron plates, 10g stone bricks, 2g clay slurry, 5g induction coils, and 5g electric motors.

intermediate processing a.name: Intermediate Processing A
intermediate processing a.text:
Now that you are able to refine raw metals like iron and copper, you will now need machines that process them into base components more efficiently rather than relying on metal wire and your printer.

The roller press is the machine you will use to shape malleable metals into flat plates and sheets
intermediate processing a.hint: The roller press requires iron plates, iron gears, induction coils, and electric motors.

intermediate processing b.name: Intermediate Processing B
intermediate processing b.text:
Now that you are able to refine raw metals like iron and copper, you will now need machines that process them into base components more efficiently rather than relying on metal wire and your printer.

The component mold shapes molten metal into shaped molds to create solid, fixed components like gears.
intermediate processing b.hint: The component mold requires iron plates, induction coils, and electric motors.

intermediate processing c.name: Intermediate Processing C
intermediate processing c.text:
Now that you are able to refine raw metals like iron and copper, you will now need machines that process them into base components more efficiently rather than relying on metal wire and your printer.

The extruder like your smelter extruder forces ductile metal through a narrow opening to create thin, round wire and rods.
intermediate processing c.hint: The extruder requires iron plates, induction coils, and electric motors.

machine maintenance.name: Machine Maintenance
machine maintenance.text:
By this point, one of your machines may have stopped working. Whether or not any have, you will need to regularly perform maintenance on your machines.

You can do this by putting a machine in maintenance mode then press the "Diagnostic" button. It will then produce a list of components that will need to be repaired and replaced. Once you have produced the necessary components (at least partially), then press the "Repair" button. The components will be used up, and the broken parts will be set aside as scrap.

You are advised to not throw away any scrap as it can be recycled usually by putting it in a smelter. It is important to conserve and reuse whatever resources you have especially this early in developing your industrial base. And as a precaution, you should reserve some components that are commonly used.
machine maintenance.hint: Pick a machine and click the "Mantenance" tab. Click the "Diagnostics" button to generate a list of components that need repair. Once you have any or all the components necessary, click "Repair". The components are consumed, and the broken parts are stored as scrap. The SRG should have been used frequently, so check that first especially since it is your most critical machine right now.

blowing glass.name: Blowing Glass
blowing glass.text:
Sand is an aggrigate of quartz or silica (silicon oxide). There will be many more purposes for it later, but for now we will focus on creating glass. Gravel was also created from crushing rock, but we will find uses for it too later.

Return to your smelter-extruder and process the sand through it. Much like your ores, it will be extruded as fine glass filament which also has many uses itself, but we will focus on using it as an intermediate material.
blowing glass.hint: Set your smelter-extruder to produce glass filament.

a huge pane.name: A Huge Pane
a huge pane.text:
Much like metal wire, the glass filament can be used in your component printer to produce static parts out of it. Glass panes can be used as transparent windows for machines or structures.

Set your component printer to produce glass panes and feed glass filament into it.
a huge pane.hint: Set the component printer to produce glass panes.

splitting water.name: Splitting Water
splitting water.text:
Water would be a vital resource to support life, but you are not prepared to support a colony of humans or other living organisms. But there are many other utilities for water, particularly the components of water, hydrogen and oxygen. Water isn't as plentiful on this planet as it would be on naturally life sustaining worlds, but there are deposits of it in the form of ice.

The first step you will need to do is harvest ice from a nearby deposit. If you constructed an automated miner, you can set it to collect ice. You can then melt it in the smelter-extruder and collect the water. Finally, you will need another machine in the form of an electrolyzer.

Collect water and report back after you've constructed the electrolyzer.

equivalent exchange.name: Equivalent Exchange
equivalent exchange.text:
You are starting to become a modern day alchemist, breaking down substances to make other desired substances. While chemistry is more complicated than alchemy requiring special equipment to force chemical reactions, it is accessible to anyone without supernatural talents as well as being more stable and carries less risk of producing warp phenomena. It is generally understood that exploiting the known physical laws of the universe is safer than methods that work around them. You should know that the planet you are on is in wild space far from civilized territory, and it is wise to be safe.

In the next steps, you will able to use elements and compounds to produce useful chemicals.
equivalent exchange.hint: In order to proceed, you will need to complete the quests "From Thin Air" and "Splitting Water".

chemistry 101.name: Chemistry 101
chemistry 101.text: The first chemical reaction you will learn is the Sabatier Reaction. It takes ingredients as carbon dioxide (CO2) and hydrogen (H2) and produces methane (CH4) and water (H2O). The water can then be recycled and electrolized again into its base elements to continue reacting with more atmospheric CO2. The methane can then be used to create other organic compounds or even in a combustion generator to generate electricity.
chemistry 101.hint: Build a chemical reactor with 10g iron plates, 10g copper wire, 5g copper plates, 2g induction coils, and 5g electric motors. Then set it to perform the sabatier reaction recipe.

chemistry 102.name: Chemistry 102
chemistry 102.text: Now that you have created methane from carbon dioxide, it is now possible to further isolate the carbon from hydrogen. A reaction called "pyrolysis" occurs by heating a substance in an environment without oxygen so it doesn't combust. The endothermic reaction absorbs the energy of the heat to seperate molecules into smaller molecules or base elements turning methane into pure carbon char and hydrogen.
chemistry 102.hint: Set a chemical reactor to perform "Methane Pyrolysis". It only consumes methane but is endothermic and costs a lot of energy.

chemistry 103.name: Chemistry 103
chemistry 103.text: The ultimate goal of this sequence of objectives is to achieve rudimentary electronics, and a critical substance for creating electronics is the element silicon. Fortunately, silicon is one of the most abundant elements especially in rocky crust. Up to now, you might have been using sand or silicon dioxide and to produce glass, but now you will need extract silicon from it to utilize pure silicon. The following is not the ideal method, and you will be introduced to a more efficient process once it becomes available to you, but for now you are going to reduce silicon. In an smelter, combine sand with carbon to get silicon and carbon monoxide as a biproduct. Carbon monoxide is poisonous to organics, but store it for now as you will also be able to process and recycle it later.
chemistry 103.hint: In an induction smelter, select the "Reduce Silicon" recipe and combine sand and carbon.

chemistry 201.name: Chemistry 201
chemistry 201.text: Creating plastics is an advanced practice of chemistry and will give you access to high tech materials including electronics. Plastics are made of polymers, and polymers and chains of monomers. Now that you have methane, you can process it into a simple hydrocarbon monomer called ethylene which can be used to create various polymers of polyethylene each with different purposes.
chemistry 201.hint: The chemcial reactor can synthesize methane into ethylene.

chemistry 202.name: Chemistry 202
chemistry 202.text: With ethylene as a base monomer, you can now make polyethylene, a basic plastic with versatile applications. The process of polymerization is more complicated, so you will need a more advanced machine with relays and control boards to automatically manage the process.
chemistry 202.hint: Construct a polymerizer and in it select the recipes for "Polymerize LDPE" and "Polymerize HDPE".

pottery.name: Pottery
pottery.text:
Creating and utilizing electronics relies on understanding conductors and insulators. You already use plenty of metals that can act as conductors, but you need a reliable matterial that can function as an insulator. You also have carbon, but ceramic will also fulfill the purpose as a structural base that won't conduct electronic signals.

You already made clay slurry and used it as mortar constructing an induction smelter. If you bake it, you can make ceramic.
pottery.hint: Use the induction smelter to bake clay slurry into ceramic.

basic electronic components.name: Basic Electronic Components
basic electronic components.text: Resistors and capacitors are the basic components for constructing electonic circuits. Resistors control electric currents, and capacitors store charge. Used in combination, they can be used to create some rudimentary control circuits.
basic electronic components.hint: Both resistors and capacitors are made in the parts assembler and need copper wire and ceramic. Resistors need carbon, and capacitors need copper foil which is made in the roller press.

clean your plate.name: Clean Your Plate
clean your plate.text: Electonics are typically assembled onto a board that is rigid and won't conduct circuits where they shouldn't and would short circuit. You can make a base insulating substrate with glass panes and ceramic in the roller press.
clean your plate.hint: In the roller press, select the recipe "Laminate Substrate" to combine glass panes and ceramic into an insulating substrate.

crude electronics.name: Crude Electronics
crude electronics.text: With basic electronic components and an insulating substrate, you can now create a simple electronic circuit board. It will function well enough for the purposes you need until you find more valuable resources and can process them into improved and more complicated components.
crude electronics.hint: Use the parts assembler to combine resistors, capacitors, and insulating substrates into control boards.

relay race.name: Relay Race
relay race.text: You have a control board, but in order to properly do anything, you need something that can turn things on or off. Something that does that is an electromagnetic relay which when it receives a signal generates an electromagnetic field that closes another circuit and turn a device on acting as an automatic switch.
relay race.hint: In the parts assembler, use copper wire, magnets, and iron plates to create relays.

logistics pt1.name: Logistics Part I
logistics pt1.text:
As stated earlier, your ship landed in a location with resource deposits critical to get started, but to gain access to more advanced technology, you will need to find rarer, more valuable resources. When you do explore and find other resources, you will need to find some way to transport large volumes of resources. Rather than carrying it all yourself, you can set up logistics networks to automatically transport it for you.

The first structure you will need to construct is a logistics hub which will be able to process resources imports and exports between regions. The other is a bus of conveyers that will carry resources on them between adjacent regions. Conveyer busses can transport solid materials, but to effectively transport liquids and gasses, you will need pipes. When you find another resource deposit, construct hubs at that region and your base and connect the two with conveyer busses. You will of course need to personally carry the necessary construction materials first.
logistics pt1.hint: If you haven't already, use the navigations buttons on the Base tab to explore neighboring regions and travel between adjacent ones. To have a logistics network function, you will need a hub in the orign and destination regions. Use the Android tab to transfer resources between the region's stockpile and your inventory. Connect regions with conveyer busses and make sure to select the target region.

mineral rush.name: Mineral Rush
mineral rush.text:
You have been working on creating electronics, but the mineral deposits around your initial landing zone are only going to get you so far, and more advanced electronics and automation will require transistors which need combinations of silicon doped with special impurities. Common elements you can utilize are boron and phosphorus to dope your silicon.

As you explore, you will need to keep an eye out for boron ore and phosphate ore. If you find any veins, you can either mine them manually or construct an automated miner. Then build a set of logistics hubs and conveyers connecting the region to your base and load the ore to be transported or carry it over yourself. Once you have either transported the ore to your base or constructed any machines at the site, refine it into boron and silicon to get ready to dope it with silicon.
mineral rush.hint: Explore regions around for deposits of boron and phosphate. After you mine it and want to transport it automatically between regions, construct logistics hubs in your base and near the deposits and conveyer busses between the regions.

dont be a dope.name: Don't be a Dope
dont be a dope.text:
Silicon is a unique metaloid semiconductor, and its valence electrons give it properties that made it critical to the advancement of the information age. However, for certain advanced electronics, silicon will be more useful by ironically doping it with certain impurities, specifically ones from elemental groups adjacent to it on the periodic table. The ones you will be working with are boron and phosphorus.

Use the smelter to combine boron with a small amount of each element to create p-doped and n-doped silicon. Combinations of both of these materials will be used to create transistors and other advanced electronics.
dont be a dope.hint: Refine boron and phospate ores into boron and phosphorus, then dope both of them with silicon in the smelter.

better than tubes.name: Better Than Tubes
better than tubes.text: The most important component of computers is the transistor. With advanced technology, you will not have to use vacuum tubes which are by all considerations worse than transistors which are much smaller and cooler. By using certain combinations of transistors and other components, you can create logic gates and even arithmetic functions.
better than tubes.hint: Use doped silicon to construct transistors in the parts assembler.

salty miner.name: Salty Miner
salty miner.text:
Salts are a broad category of chemicals, usually formed from combining an alkaline metal with a halogen, but the salt most commonly referred to by simply "salt" would be table salt or sodium chloride (NaCl). Table salt is frequently used for flavoring or preserving food, but it also has a lot of utility in chemistry especially if it is broken down into its base elements or other chemicals.

Explore nearby regions for salt deposits and mine them manually or with an automated miner. Then either carry it back or transport it through a logistics network of hubs and conveyers.
salty miner.hint: Explore nearby regions for salt deposits. They are more likely in flat plains which could potentially have been sea beds.

not gonna lye.name: Not Gonna Lye
not gonna lye.text: To use the base elements of NaCl salt, you will need to break it down chemically. Like you did with regular water before, you can again electrolyze a mix of salt water to create biproducts of sodium hydroxide (NaOH), or lye soda, and chlorine.
not gonna lye.hint: In a mixer, combine salt with water to make salt water. Then use the electrolyzer to electrolize it.

basics of acid.name: Basics of Acid
basics of acid.text: A commonly used acid you can make with the resources available to you is hydrochloric acid (HCl). It is highly corrosive which makes it dangerous but useful if that's what you require.
basics of acid.hint: Set a chemical reactor to synthesize hydrochloric acid using hydrogen and chlorine.

a bath wont kill you.name: A Bath Won't Kill You
a bath wont kill you.text: To make custom circuit boards, you can use a chemical etching solution to create a specific pattern in a prepared copper substrate board. An etching solution will be used to remove copper from exposed sections of the board to leave precise circuits. Use the mixer to combine copper foil with HCl acid and oxygen to make the necessary etching solution. Then construct an etching bath to be used to submerge the boards.
a bath wont kill you.hint: In a mixer, combine copper foil, HCl acid, and oxygen. Then construct an etching bath machine.

better boards.name: Better Boards
better boards.text: Computer circuit boards will require precise circuits printed on boards to assemble electronics on. The machines available to you now aren't precise enough to create something that intricately detailed, but until then, you can etch it into your boards. Before then, you will need to prepare boards with thin circuits of copper to carry the signals. Use the roller press to press thin sheets of copper foil and polyethylene onto laminate substrate.
better boards.hint: Use the roller press with laminate substrate with copper foil and low-density polyethylene. Copper foil can also be made in the roller press.

a quick soak.name: A Quick Soak
a quick soak.text: Submerging the prepared copper-clad boards with a protective layer in an intended pattern will leave the copper circuits on the board, and it will be ready for other electronic components to be assembled onto it. The copper etched from the board will then be leached into the solution, but that could then be regenerated into usable etching solution. Process the spent etchent solution in the mixer with HCl acid and oxigen to regenerate it into fresh etching solution.
a quick soak.hint: Use the etching bath to turn copper-clad substrates into printed circuit boards. Some of the etching solution will turn into spent etchent which can be regenerated in the mixer.

improved electronics.name: Improved Electronics
improved electronics.text: With transistors and a proper printed circuit board, you can now assemble boards used in more advanced computering hardware. These can then be programmed for smarter automation.
improved electronics.hint: In a parts assembler, craft transistors, resistors, and capacitors with printed circuit boards.
